fallos_mitigaciones: Prior systems (append-only vector stores) never filter at ingestion, retrieve by cosine similarity alone, and accumulate stale/contradictory facts indefinitely (Abstract, Sec.1). Mitigated by: SurprisalGate filters low-information inputs at write time (reduces stored noise by 40% at default threshold tau=0.3, Sec.5.1, Fig.2); MutableRAG flags retrieved chunks as labile and reconsolidates them, 'solving the stale-fact problem' via version-incremented in-place overwrite with a 60s cooldown and 10-version audit trail (Sec.3.2, Sec.5.4 -- stale React fact updates to Svelte only when reconsolidation is enabled); a write-safety firewall detects/blocks/redacts secrets and PII at every write path (Sec.7).

fallos_mitigaciones: 'Silent inconsistency': when memories accumulate across sessions/sources, 'no existing system provides a formal guarantee for detecting such contradictions. Instead, systems silently serve whichever memory the similarity metric ranks highest, regardless of logical consistency' (Sec.1, open problem 3). Mitigated by modeling the memory store as a cellular sheaf over a graph of memory contexts, where non-trivial first cohomology classes H1(F)!=0 provide 'an algebraic consistency guarantee' that formally flags irreconcilable contradictions across contexts (Sec.2.6, Sec.5.4) -- the first such guarantee reported for agent memory.

fallos_mitigaciones: Concurrent belief updates cause silent or unresolvable conflicts in prior systems: 'if an agent's memory contains "client prefers warm tones" and a concurrent write produces "client now prefers cool tones", Letta's system generates a text-level merge conflict requiring human or LLM intervention' (Sec.'Related Work'). Mitigated by AGM-compliant belief revision operators: a Supersedes edge creates a new immutable revision with formal guarantees (Success, Consistency, minimal change via Relevance), moves the tag pointer, and makes the stale belief retrievable only via explicit opt-in, with AnalyzeImpact automatically propagating the change to downstream dependent conclusions via typed Depends_On edges. On LoCoMo-Plus, two consolidation enrichments (prospective indexing + event extraction) eliminated a '>6-month accuracy cliff (37.5% -> 84.4%)', and 78% of remaining end-to-end failures are attributable to answer-model fabrication over correctly-retrieved context, not retrieval failure, since 'the memory graph contains no fabricated information, so there is nothing for the model to hallucinate from' (Abstract).

fallos_mitigaciones: False memory accumulation and semantic drift across extended sessions are the paper's central problem: uncontrolled retention/interference degrades persona consistency and factual stability, and the false memory rate (FMR) is explicitly tracked as a failure metric (Sec.I, Table.II-IV). Mitigated by the retention-stability regularizer L_ret (Eq.9), which penalizes abrupt shifts in the semantic-memory entity embedding between consecutive sessions to prevent catastrophic forgetting; Table.V ablation shows removing this term (-Lret) raises FMR from 5.1% to 6.5% and lowers 6-period retention from 56.90% to 52.98%, confirming the mitigation's measured contribution.

fallos_mitigaciones: Embedding-based retrieval misses goal-relevant content because raw text 'doesn't use goal vocabulary': the example 'agreed to 15% discount after client mentioned competitors' would not surface for a risk-exposure query since it lacks risk terminology, because 'embedding-based retrieval matches on semantic similarity, not goal-relevance' (Sec.1). Mitigated by goal-conditioned encoding at write time (perspectives preserve what matters for their own goals rather than deferring all interpretation to retrieval). The architecture also explicitly guards against indiscriminate peer-critique collapse ('a perspective that attacks everything degrades the system into trivial mutual conflict', analogous to semantic drift/logical deterioration reported in unconstrained multi-agent debate systems) via prompt-level selectivity/contextuality constraints -- though the authors state this reliability property 'is not guaranteed by the architecture, and is the open empirical question' (Sec.3, Observations and Limitations).

fallos_mitigaciones: The 'static-dynamic dilemma': existing systems resort to (i) destructive overwriting, which 'permanently erases historical context'; (ii) LLM arbitration at every ingestion step, which is 'infeasible when scaling to long-term memory with millions of facts'; or (iii) recency sorting, which 'silently buries static knowledge' -- e.g. ranking the decades-old-but-permanent fact (Obama, born_in, Hawaii) below fresher but irrelevant entries (Sec.1). Mitigated by a Semantic Speed Gate (per-relation volatility score alpha_r) combined with continuous phase rotation ('geometric shadowing'): static relations (alpha_r~0) stay permanently in phase while dynamic relations (alpha_r~1) rotate to shadow obsolete facts, resolving conflicts at query time without deleting the append-only memory. On MultiTQ, this raises MRR from HippoRAG's 0.203 to 0.337 and LLM@5 accuracy from 0.112 to 0.366 (Sec.4.3), while DMR-MSC confirms zero degradation of static/non-temporal retrieval (MRR 0.856 vs HippoRAG baseline 0.848).
